seo.title: Homeless help in San Diego - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in San Diego: shelter access, meals, hygiene, health care, benefits, work, documents, legal help, and specialist support.

page.heading: San Diego homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, fire, overdose, or medical emergency: 911 Shelter, outreach, food, and local services: 211 City Homeless Outreach Team: 619-446-1010 Mental-health or substance-use crisis: call or text 988, or call 888-724-7240 Domestic violence: 619-234-3164 or 888-385-4657
page.notice: Beds, meals, funding, hours, eligibility, and referral routes can change. Call or check the linked provider page before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, payment, document, benefit, ride, or job. Call 911 for immediate danger or a life-threatening medical emergency.
page.intro:
San Diego uses coordinated shelter intake. Many City-funded shelters do not accept unscheduled walk-ins. Call 211 and ask for a City of San Diego outreach specialist, or start in person at Father Joe's Villages Day Center. Tell staff your exact location, age, household members, immediate safety, medical or mobility needs, pregnancy, veteran status, whether you are living in a vehicle, and whether you have a service animal or pet.
Best first step for a single adult: call 211, or visit the San Diego Day Center at 1501 Imperial Avenue. The Day Center publishes daily hours of 7:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m. and can begin an assessment, place you on a shelter waitlist, and connect you with showers, laundry, mail, charging, meals, health care, and documents. A visit does not reserve a bed.
page.footer: No Home Help — free, static information without tracking.

categories.title: Urgent help, outreach, and bad weather

entries.title: Emergency services — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911. Text 911 if calling would place you in danger and text-to-911 is available.
Call for immediate violence, fire, overdose, unconsciousness, severe breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, serious injury, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first.
City of San Diego — assistance directory

entries.title: 211 San Diego — shelter and local-service referral
entries.description:
Call: 211, 24 hours a day. Interpretation is available in many languages.
Ask for shelter access, a City outreach specialist, food, health care, benefits, safe parking, or another local service. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and state whether you are alone, with children, under 25, a veteran, escaping violence, living in a vehicle, or have a disability. A referral does not guarantee a bed.
211 San Diego — housing and homelessness

entries.title: Homeless Outreach Team
entries.description:
Phone: 619-446-1010.
The San Diego Police Department's Homeless Outreach Team can connect willing participants with shelter, detoxification, treatment, and other services. For non-police street outreach, call 211 and request a City outreach specialist. Outreach cannot guarantee a placement.
City of San Diego — outreach contacts

entries.title: The Hub — navigation by appointment
entries.description:
The Hub can provide short-term navigation, housing search support, employment readiness, basic-needs connections, family reunification, and diversion from the shelter system. Calling 211 starts a referral; it does not guarantee housing or shelter.
City of San Diego — The Hub
entries.how_to_access: Access: call 211 for a referral. In-person navigator meetings are by appointment.

entries.title: 988 and San Diego Access and Crisis Line
entries.description:
Call or text: 988. Local line: 888-724-7240, 24 hours, free and confidential.
For suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, or a mental-health or substance-use crisis. A clinician-led Mobile Crisis Response Team may be sent when appropriate. Call 911 for immediate physical danger or a medical emergency.
County of San Diego — get behavioral-health help

entries.title: Inclement Weather Shelter Program
entries.description:
The City may activate additional overnight beds during cold, rain, strong wind, or other severe weather, generally from November through March. Activated beds are usually first come, first served and available for one night.
Check the live City page or call 211 on the day you need shelter. Do not travel to a weather bed unless activation and location are confirmed.
City of San Diego — inclement-weather status

entries.title: A practical plan for today
entries.description:
1. If there is immediate danger or a life-threatening medical problem: call 911 and give the exact location first.
2. If you need a safe place tonight: call 211 and ask for a City outreach specialist. State your household type, age, safety, medical needs, vehicle, veteran status, and animal.
3. If you are a single adult downtown: go early to the San Diego Day Center, 1501 Imperial Avenue. Ask for shelter assessment, an orange badge, lunch, shower, laundry, mail, and document help.
4. If you have children, are under 25, are a veteran, or are escaping violence: use the specialist route in this page. Do not accept a general-adult referral without stating your circumstances.
5. Apply for benefits: call ACCESS at 866-262-9881 or visit the Metro Family Resource Center. Ask about expedited CalFresh, Medi-Cal, and General Relief.
6. Protect your next steps: register a safe mailing address, replace ID, keep copies of every notice, and write down the name, date, and outcome of each call.

entries.title: City coordinated shelter intake
entries.description:
Start with: 211 or a City outreach worker.
The City system includes programs for adults, families, women, young people, veterans, older adults, and people with behavioral-health needs. Outreach and intake staff match people to available and appropriate beds. Most programs are referral based and cannot promise same-day placement.
San Diego Housing Commission — current shelter system

entries.title: San Diego Day Center — adults and single-adult shelter waitlist
entries.description:
Phone: 619-233-8500. Published hours: daily, 7:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
Adults can ask for an assessment, shelter waitlist, housing resources, showers, laundry, mail, charging, and a meal badge. Bring ID, income records, and medications if you have them. Father Joe's Villages says it will help begin the process if documents are missing.
Father Joe's Villages — get help
entries.address: Address: 1501 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101; enter from Commercial Street onto 15th Street

entries.title: Joan Kroc Center — adults with children
entries.description:
Phone: 619-233-8500. Published front-desk hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–12:45 p.m. and 1:15–4:30 p.m.
Families can ask about shelter, assessment, and housing resources. Bring children's birth certificates and proof of income if available, but ask staff for help if they are missing. A visit does not guarantee placement.
Father Joe's Villages — family access
entries.address: Address: 1501 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: Alpha Project bridge shelters — adults
entries.description:
Information: 619-542-1877.
Alpha Project operates City-funded adult bridge shelters with case management and housing navigation. Intake uses coordinated assessment and referral; these are not reliable public walk-in beds. Call 211 for outreach and referral.
Alpha Project — bridge shelters

entries.title: Alpha Project Family Shelter
entries.description:
City-funded interim shelter for families with children. The program uses Coordinated Entry and provides temporary housing and support toward longer-term housing. Email is also listed on the official page, but calling 211 is the clearest starting route.
Alpha Project — Family Shelter
entries.how_to_access: Access: call 211 and ask for an outreach-team referral.

entries.title: Rachel's Night Shelter — women
entries.description:
Phone: 619-696-0873.
Emergency and short-term shelter for adult women, with bathrooms, showers, laundry, evening meals, clothing, storage, a mailing address, and support. Call for current intake and capacity; a call does not reserve a bed.
Catholic Charities — homeless women's services

entries.title: Rachel's Promise — women and families with children
entries.description:
Phone: 619-473-2400.
City-funded shelter and supportive services operated by Catholic Charities. Published services include meals, showers, laundry, clothing, mail, behavioral-health support, and resource navigation. Call about intake and vacancies.
Catholic Charities — Rachel's Promise | SDHC shelter list — https://sdhc.org/homelessness-solutions/city-homeless-shelters-services/

entries.title: Storefront Youth Emergency Shelter — ages 12–17
entries.description:
24-hour screening: 866-752-2327.
Emergency night shelter and drop-in support for minors who have no safe living arrangement or are running away. Telephone screening is required. The program can provide shelter, showers, laundry, meals, case management, and help returning safely to family or another placement.
San Diego Youth Services — shelter information

entries.title: Safe STAY Wellness Center — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Bed and vacancy inquiry: 619-694-6182.
LGBTQ-affirming shelter for unhoused young adults, with meals, showers, laundry, peer support, case management, and housing connections. Ask about current vacancies and intake before traveling.
San Diego LGBT Community Center — housing services

entries.title: TAY Emergency Shelter — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Urban Street Angels operates City-funded shelter beds for transition-age youth. Intake and bed status can change.
Call 211 and state your age clearly. Ask for a youth-specific outreach or shelter referral rather than a general adult placement.
SDHC — current youth shelters

entries.title: City-funded Veterans Shelter
entries.description:
Veterans Village of San Diego operates City-funded beds for adult veterans. Intake is coordinated and availability changes.
Call 877-424-3838 for the national VA homeless-veteran line, or 619-393-2000 for Veterans Village program entry. Do not travel expecting a bed without confirmation.
SDHC — Veterans Shelter | Veterans Village of San Diego — https://vvsd.net/

entries.title: Jewish Family Service Safe Parking — people living in vehicles
entries.description:
Secured lots operate nightly, with case management and housing support. Some sites accept larger vehicles; rules and availability differ by lot.
Apply through the provider and do not arrive without enrollment. Ask about vehicle registration, insurance, pets, household members, arrival times, and lot rules.
Jewish Family Service — Safe Parking Program

entries.title: San Diego Rescue Mission — South County Lighthouse
entries.description:
Referral information: 619-819-1842.
Free 30-day emergency shelter in National City for men, women, and families. The provider says entry is by referral and up to two pets may be accepted. Call to confirm eligibility, referral steps, and capacity.
San Diego Rescue Mission — get help

entries.title: Franklin Antonio Public Lunch Program
entries.description:
Phone: 619-233-8500. Published meal: Monday–Saturday, 11:00 a.m.–12:30 p.m.; Sunday, 9:30–11:30 a.m.
Free public meal every day. First-time visitors need an orange service badge from the Day Center or Joan Kroc Center front desk. Arrive in the morning to obtain the badge and confirm the line and schedule.
Father Joe's Villages — public lunch
entries.address: Address: 1501 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101; courtyard on 15th Street

entries.title: Father Joe's Villages food pantry
entries.description:
Published distribution: Friday, 11:30 a.m.–2:00 p.m.
Drive-through pantry with shelf-stable food and, when available, produce, milk, and bread. The schedule can change around holidays; confirm before traveling. Ask whether walk-up access is possible if you have no vehicle.
Father Joe's Villages — food pantry
entries.address: Address: 3350 E Street, San Diego, CA 92102; follow signs to the back

entries.title: Feeding San Diego — live food map
entries.description:
Search by ZIP code and filter for walk-up sites and distributions open now. Individual sites set their own schedules and eligibility rules, and holiday or weather closures can occur.
Feeding San Diego — find free food

entries.title: Jacobs & Cushman San Diego Food Bank
entries.description:
Food locator help: 866-350-3663, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Use the live map to find a distribution by ZIP code and day. Review each site's description for eligibility, closures, registration, and what to bring before traveling.
San Diego Food Bank — get food

entries.title: Abundant Grace Christian Center
entries.description:
Phone: 619-788-2027. Feeding San Diego lists walk-up distributions on Monday morning, Wednesday evening, and Sunday late morning.
This is a Christian church site. Confirm the current times on the live food map; the listing does not say that worship is required.
Feeding San Diego — current listing
entries.address: Address: 5858 El Cajon Boulevard, San Diego, CA 92115

entries.title: 31st Street Seventh-day Adventist Church
entries.description:
Feeding San Diego lists a walk-up food distribution on the second and fourth Wednesday of the month, 12:00–2:00 p.m.
This is a Seventh-day Adventist church site. Confirm the date before traveling; the food listing does not state that worship is required.
Feeding San Diego — current listing
entries.address: Address: 414 S. 31st Street, San Diego, CA 92113

entries.title: Bayview Baptist Church — Daily Bread Marketplace
entries.description:
Phone: 619-262-8384. Feeding San Diego lists weekday-morning food by appointment.
This is a Baptist church program. Call first for an appointment, current hours, and eligibility. Do not assume same-day food without confirmation.
Feeding San Diego — current listing
entries.address: Address: 6126 Pastor Timothy J. Winters Street, San Diego, CA 92114

entries.title: Church of the Nazarene food distribution
entries.description:
Phone: 619-516-1000. Feeding San Diego lists weekly Tuesday-afternoon and Saturday-morning walk-up distributions.
This is a Christian church site. Confirm the current schedule on the live map; no worship requirement is stated in the food listing.
Feeding San Diego — current listing
entries.address: Address: 4101 University Avenue, San Diego, CA 92105

entries.title: City Heights Assembly of God — hot meals
entries.description:
Phone: 619-471-4809. Feeding San Diego lists weekday hot meals for families with children under 18 or adults age 65+.
Call before traveling to confirm eligibility, meal times, and whether the program is operating that day.
Feeding San Diego — current listing
entries.address: Address: 3737 Wightman Street, San Diego, CA 92105

entries.title: Serving Seniors — downtown meals for older adults
entries.description:
Phone: 619-235-6572.
Serving Seniors publishes breakfast and lunch service at this location. Registration or age rules may apply. Call for today's meal times, eligibility, and accessibility before traveling.
Serving Seniors — locations and meals
entries.address: Address: Gary and Mary West Senior Wellness Center, 1525 4th Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

categories.title: Showers, laundry, clothing, mail, and storage

entries.title: San Diego Day Center
entries.description:
Phone: 619-233-8500. Published hours: daily, 7:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
Restrooms, showers, laundry, mail, phone charging, computer access, and navigation for adults experiencing or at risk of homelessness. An orange badge is required for services; obtain it at the Day Center or Joan Kroc Center. Individual lines and service hours may end earlier than the building hours.
Father Joe's Villages — Day Center
entries.address: Address: 1501 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: Rachel's Women's Center and Rachel's Promise
entries.description:
Rachel's Promise: 619-473-2400. Night Shelter: 619-696-0873.
Services for women can include showers, laundry, clothing, meals, mail, storage, behavioral-health support, and shelter screening. Call for the correct location, current access rules, and service hours.
Catholic Charities — women's services

entries.title: Transitional Storage Center — downtown
entries.description:
Free lockers and bins for adults experiencing homelessness in the City. Enrollment requires self-certifying homelessness, accepting facility rules, and checking in regularly. Food, medication, weapons, animals, and some other items cannot be stored.
City of San Diego — storage rules | Think Dignity — storage program — https://thinkdignity.org/programs/impact-services/
entries.address: Address: 252 16th Street, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: Storage Connect Center — Logan Heights
entries.description:
Free storage bins for adults experiencing homelessness who reside in the City. Ask about enrollment, waitlist, bin size, weekly check-in, and current hours before bringing belongings.
SDHC — storage centers
entries.address: Address: 116 S. 20th Street, San Diego, CA 92113

entries.title: Storage Connect Center — Chollas Creek
entries.description:
Free storage bins for adults experiencing homelessness in the City. The same City rules apply: enrollment, terms of service, regular check-in, and restrictions on what may be stored.
City of San Diego — storage centers
entries.address: Address: 5453 Lea Street, San Diego, CA 92105

entries.title: Think Dignity — ID Bank and outreach supplies
entries.description:
Phone: 619-537-8736.
The ID Bank helps obtain and securely store birth certificates, Social Security cards, and California IDs. Think Dignity also publishes an outreach calendar for clothing, hygiene supplies, and legal services. Check the current calendar before traveling.
Think Dignity — impact services | current outreach calendar — https://thinkdignity.org/support/

entries.title: San Diego Central Library
entries.description:
Indoor public space during library hours, restrooms subject to library rules, free Wi-Fi, computers, charging where outlets are available, printing, scanning, and staff referral. Verify today's opening hours before traveling.
San Diego Public Library — internet and computers
entries.address: Address: 330 Park Boulevard, San Diego, CA 92101

categories.title: Health, dental, mental health, and substance-use help

entries.title: Village Health Center — Father Joe's Villages
entries.description:
Clinic: 619-645-6405.
Primary care, dental care, behavioral health, psychiatry, and substance-use services for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Walk-in times differ by service. Call or visit early to ask about same-day care, cost, identification, insurance, and medication needs.
Father Joe's Villages — health services
entries.address: Address: 1501 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: Family Health Centers of San Diego — Healthcare for the Homeless
entries.description:
Appointments and information: 619-515-2477.
No referral is required for homeless services. Clinics offer primary care, dental, vision, mental health, substance-use services, HIV and hepatitis care, case management, transport support, and Medi-Cal enrollment. Ask for the nearest clinic and current walk-in options.
Family Health Centers — homeless services

entries.title: Downtown Family Health Center at Connections
entries.description:
Scheduling line: 619-515-2477.
Downtown clinic within the Family Health Centers network. Call for the current address, hours, walk-in status, and services before traveling. A clinic can also help with insurance enrollment and referrals.
Family Health Centers — locations and homeless care

entries.title: San Diego County Psychiatric Hospital
entries.description:
Walk-in emergency information: 619-692-8232. The County describes adult psychiatric emergency services as available 24 hours.
For an urgent behavioral-health crisis when you can travel safely. Call or text 988 first for guidance when possible. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.
County of San Diego — crisis facilities
entries.address: Address: 3853 Rosecrans Street, San Diego, CA 92110

entries.title: Mobile Crisis Response Team
entries.description:
Call or text: 988, or call 888-724-7240.
County teams can respond to mental-health or substance-use crises that do not require an immediate police, fire, or ambulance response. Dispatch depends on assessment and safety. Support is free, confidential, and available in many languages.
County of San Diego — crisis services

entries.title: Substance-use treatment navigation
entries.description:
Phone: 888-724-7240, 24 hours.
Ask the Access and Crisis Line for detoxification, outpatient, residential, medication-assisted treatment, or harm-reduction services. State what substance is involved, the last use, withdrawal symptoms, pregnancy, medications, insurance, and whether you need a bed. Call 911 for overdose, unconsciousness, seizures, or severe breathing trouble.
San Diego Access and Crisis Line

entries.title: Medi-Cal enrollment help at clinics
entries.description:
Family Health Centers says certified enrollment staff are available at its clinics to help apply for Medi-Cal or other coverage. Bring identification and income information if available, but ask what alternatives can be used if documents are missing.
Family Health Centers — enrollment support

entries.title: Health-coverage legal help
entries.description:
Consumer Center: 877-734-3258, Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Free help with Medi-Cal, Medicare, Covered California, denied care, medical bills, equipment, medications, and appeals for eligible San Diego County residents.
Legal Aid Society — health care and coverage

entries.title: PRONTO LIFE — reduced fare for benefit recipients
entries.description:
People actively enrolled in CalFresh, Medi-Cal, or CalWORKs may apply for PRONTO LIFE if they are not already using another reduced-fare category. MTS publishes a $2.50 one-way fare, $6 daily cap, and $72 monthly cap for eligible regional bus and Trolley travel.
PRONTO support: 619-595-5636. A current County benefits-verification letter, valid ID, application, and release form are required. Fares and rules can change.
MTS — PRONTO LIFE

entries.title: Senior, disability, and Medicare reduced fares
entries.description:
Reduced fares are available to qualifying riders age 65+, people with disabilities, and Medicare recipients. Accepted proof varies. Apply online, through PRONTO support, or at the MTS Transit Store.
Transit Store: 1255 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101. Support: 619-595-5636.
MTS — reduced-fare eligibility

entries.title: Youth Opportunity Pass
entries.description:
MTS says riders age 18 and under can ride free with an approved Youth PRONTO account or card through June 30, 2027. Proof of age or school enrollment is required to set up the youth fare.
Ask a youth service provider or PRONTO support for help if documents are missing.
MTS — youth fare information

entries.title: San Diego Public Library computers and Wi-Fi
entries.description:
Library computers provide internet and office applications. A library or Internet card is required; standard sessions are 60 minutes and more sessions depend on availability. Wi-Fi is free at all branches during opening hours.
Printing costs money. Ask staff about a card, scanning, job-search assistance, and the nearest open branch.
Library internet access | free Wi-Fi — https://www.sandiego.gov/public-library/services/specialresources/internet/wireless

entries.title: SD Access 4 All — devices and digital help
entries.description:
Digital Navigators: 800-350-6945.
Participating libraries lend Chromebooks and mobile hotspots for limited periods, subject to availability and library-card requirements. Digital Navigators can help with low-cost devices, internet service, and basic technical support.
San Diego Public Library — Access 4 All

entries.title: Day Center phone charging and computer access
entries.description:
Adults with an orange badge can ask about phone charging, computer access, mail, and employment or education resources. Lines and availability vary; keep your device with you and ask staff before leaving it to charge.
Father Joe's Villages — Day Center
entries.address: Address: 1501 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: Traveler's Aid — reunification travel
entries.description:
Phone: 619-233-8500, extension 1157.
May help with transportation to another place where safe, stable housing has been verified. Assistance depends on assessment and funding. Bring the receiving person's contact details and be prepared for staff to verify the destination.
Father Joe's Villages — other services
entries.address: Start at: 1501 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: MTS Route 992 — downtown to San Diego International Airport
entries.description:
Route 992 connects downtown stops near Broadway and Kettner Boulevard with airport terminals. Standard MTS fares apply. Check the live timetable and terminal stops before leaving.
The Trolley does not stop directly at the airport. Use Santa Fe Depot, America Plaza, or Courthouse stations to connect with Route 992.
San Diego International Airport — public transportation

entries.title: San Diego Flyer — airport to Middletown Trolley
entries.description:
The airport's shuttle connects Terminals 1 and 2 with the Admiral Boland Way stop, about one block from Middletown Station on the Blue and Green Trolley lines. Check the airport page for current operating times.
Airport — Trolley connection

entries.title: Do not buy a ticket before housing is confirmed
entries.description:
If someone in another city offers a place to stay, ask Traveler's Aid or a case manager to verify the address, contact person, length of stay, and arrival plan. Do not spend your last money on travel based only on a message or verbal promise.
Traveler's Aid: 619-233-8500, extension 1157.

entries.title: ACCESS Customer Service Center
entries.description:
Phone: 866-262-9881. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; TTY 711.
Apply for or ask about CalFresh, Medi-Cal, CalWORKs, General Relief, CAPI, and other County programs. Ask how to document homelessness, where to collect an EBT card, and how to submit missing verification.
County of San Diego — ACCESS

entries.title: Metro Family Resource Center
entries.description:
Phone: 866-262-9881. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
In-person eligibility and document submission for CalFresh, Medi-Cal, and General Relief. Ask whether an appointment is required and what identification or alternatives are accepted.
County of San Diego — Metro FRC
entries.address: Address: 1130 10th Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: BenefitsCal — online applications and document uploads
entries.description:
Apply online for CalFresh, Medi-Cal, CalWORKs, and General Relief. Save the application number and upload requested documents. Use a trusted device, sign out, and do not save passwords on a public computer.
BenefitsCal | County help — https://benefitscal.com/

entries.title: Expedited CalFresh
entries.description:
Some households with very little income and cash, or whose income and cash are less than shelter and utility costs, may qualify for expedited food benefits within three days after applying. Approval is not automatic.
Tell the County you are homeless and have little or no food. Identity must be verified before benefits can be issued. Ask what documents or collateral contacts can prove identity.
County of San Diego — CalFresh application

entries.title: General Relief
entries.description:
Temporary cash assistance for eligible County residents who have no other means of support. Apply through BenefitsCal, ACCESS, or a Family Resource Center.
Eligibility, work rules, repayment, and documentation can vary. Ask for a written notice if denied or discontinued so you know the reason and appeal deadline.
County of San Diego — General Relief locations

entries.title: HOUSING FIRST – SAN DIEGO hotline
entries.description:
Phone: 619-578-7768.
For City residents at imminent risk of homelessness or experiencing housing instability. Staff assess whether an available prevention or housing program fits the household. Funding and eligibility are limited; calling does not promise payment.
City of San Diego — rent and housing help

entries.title: City Eviction Prevention Program
entries.description:
Legal Aid intake: 877-534-2524, Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Free legal help for eligible low-income tenants in the City facing eviction for unpaid rent. Assistance can include advice, responses to notices or court papers, negotiation, reasonable-accommodation requests, and representation. Call immediately because court deadlines are short.
Legal Aid Society — Eviction Prevention Program

entries.title: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher waiting list
entries.description:
Phone: 619-578-7640, Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
Apply to the waiting list, check status, and update contact information. Placement can take a long time and is not emergency shelter. Keep phone, email, mailing address, and household information current.
San Diego Housing Commission — waiting list

entries.title: Affordable housing search
entries.description:
Search San Diego Housing Commission properties and the Citywide Affordable Housing Resource Guide. Contact each property directly about vacancies, income limits, accessibility, application fees, and waiting lists.
Never pay a deposit or application fee before verifying the property and written terms. Affordable housing applications are not a same-night shelter route.
San Diego Housing Commission — affordable rentals

entries.title: Metro Career Center
entries.description:
Phone: 619-319-9675. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Free walk-in job-search and career-development services for San Diego County job seekers age 16+. Ask about résumé help, interview preparation, training, certifications, paid opportunities, and priority service for veterans.
San Diego Workforce Partnership — career centers
entries.address: Address: 4389 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92113

entries.title: Workforce Partnership young-adult services
entries.description:
Young people can ask the Metro Career Center about age-specific career coaching, education, paid internships, training, and supportive services. Eligibility differs by program.
Tell staff if you lack ID, transport, interview clothing, a mailing address, or computer access so those barriers can be included in the plan.
Workforce Partnership — youth and career help

entries.title: CalJOBS
entries.description:
California's public job-search system includes job listings, résumé tools, training information, and unemployment-related services. Use a private email address and sign out on public computers.
CalJOBS

entries.title: Father Joe's Villages employment resources
entries.description:
Phone: 619-233-8500.
The Employment Center offers computers, phones, classes, and employment support, but the provider currently states that this center serves residents only. People using the Day Center can still ask staff for another employment referral.
Father Joe's Villages — employment information

entries.title: Applying without a permanent address
entries.description:
Use a shelter or service-provider mailing address only after staff registers you and confirms the exact format. A private email and reliable voicemail are often more important for applications. Keep a simple list of applications and follow-up dates.
Ask the Day Center, Metro Career Center, or library for computer access and printing. Never pay a recruiter for a job, gift cards, equipment, or a background check without independently verifying the employer.

entries.title: Legal Aid Society of San Diego
entries.description:
General intake: 877-534-2524. TTY: 800-735-2929. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Free civil legal help for eligible residents, including eviction, housing discrimination, public benefits, health coverage, SSI, family law, restraining orders, and name or gender-marker changes. The organization does not handle criminal defense.
Legal Aid Society — services

entries.title: Eviction Defense Walk-in Clinic
entries.description:
Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–3:30 p.m., except court holidays; first come, first served.
Help responding to an unlawful-detainer lawsuit or asking for more time after a sheriff's notice to vacate. Bring every notice and court paper. Deadlines can be very short, so go as soon as possible.
Legal Aid Society — walk-in clinics
entries.address: Address: Hall of Justice, 330 W. Broadway, 2nd floor, Room 251, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: Public-benefits legal help
entries.description:
Phone: 877-534-2524.
Advice and possible representation for problems with General Relief, CalWORKs, CalFresh, CAPI, or other cash and food benefits. Keep the County notice and envelope because appeal deadlines matter.
Legal Aid Society — public assistance

entries.title: Think Dignity legal services and Homeless Court referrals
entries.description:
Phone: 619-537-8736.
Dignity Legal Services publishes free community-based legal assistance and outreach. Homeless Court generally requires referral through a participating service provider and documented program participation; it is not a walk-in dismissal of tickets.
Think Dignity — legal services | outreach calendar — https://thinkdignity.org/support/

entries.title: Your Safe Place — Family Justice Center
entries.description:
Phone: 619-533-6000.
Free, confidential help for domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, trafficking, elder abuse, hate crime, and other abuse. Partners can assist with restraining orders, family court, immigration, safety planning, and referrals. Call 911 if danger is immediate.
City of San Diego — Your Safe Place

entries.title: Immigration Legal Services Coalition — urgent enforcement or detention
entries.description:
Phone: 858-751-7553. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.
Free consultation, rights information, limited-scope help, and trusted referrals for people detained by immigration enforcement or at imminent risk. Leave a message after hours. Services depend on case, eligibility, funding, and capacity.
ILSC San Diego

entries.title: Jewish Family Service immigration legal services
entries.description:
Phone: 858-637-3365.
Free immigration legal services for eligible low-income San Diego County residents, including certain DACA, citizenship, residency, humanitarian, and removal-defense matters. Call for screening; representation is not guaranteed.
Jewish Family Service — immigration programs

entries.title: Catholic Charities immigration services
entries.description:
Phone: 619-287-1270.
Low-cost immigration consultations and applications, including family petitions, citizenship, work authorization, humanitarian visas, and some removal defense. Ask about fees, language, appointment, and whether the program handles your case type.
Catholic Charities — immigrant services
entries.address: Address: 4575 B Mission Gorge Place, San Diego, CA 92120

entries.title: Encampment clean-up and property retrieval
entries.description:
The City publishes notice and storage procedures for clean-ups. Items with apparent utility, including identification, paperwork, and medication, may be stored rather than immediately discarded. A posted notice should explain retrieval.
Personal-belonging retrieval: 858-694-7000. Photograph notices and belongings when safe, keep dates, and ask Legal Aid or Think Dignity for advice if property is lost.
City of San Diego — clean-up and retrieval procedure

entries.title: California no-fee identification card
entries.description:
People who meet the federal definition of homelessness may qualify for a no-fee California ID card. A qualifying government agency or nonprofit must verify homelessness and issue form DL 933. The waiver applies to an ID card, not a driver license.
Ask the Day Center, Think Dignity, or another case manager whether they can issue the form and help gather identity and residency evidence before a DMV visit.
California DMV — no-fee ID program

entries.title: Think Dignity ID Bank
entries.description:
Phone: 619-537-8736.
Help obtaining and securely storing birth certificates, Social Security cards, and California IDs. Services are offered through scheduled outreach and partner sites; check the current calendar or email listed on the official page.
Think Dignity — ID Bank

entries.title: Replace a Social Security card
entries.description:
The Social Security Administration may allow an online replacement in some cases; others require an application and original identity documents. Replacement cards are free.
Do not pay an unofficial website. Ask a case manager or ID Bank for help if you lack identity documents, a mailing address, or online access.
Social Security Administration — replace a card

entries.title: Birth certificate
entries.description:
For a birth registered in San Diego County within the last two years, contact the County Office of Vital Records and Statistics. For older records, the County directs applicants to the Assessor/Recorder/County Clerk. Identity and notarization rules depend on the type of certified copy requested.
If cost or identification is a barrier, ask Think Dignity or a homeless-service case manager before ordering.
San Diego County — birth certificates

entries.title: Day Center mail service
entries.description:
Ask staff to register you before using the address. Confirm the exact name and address format, accepted mail, collection hours, ID rules, and how long items are held. Do not send an ID, EBT card, bank card, or legal document until staff confirms the procedure.
Father Joe's Villages — Day Center services
entries.address: Address: 1501 Imperial Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: Protecting documents
entries.description:
Photograph or scan documents and store copies in a password-protected account you can reach from another device. Keep Social Security numbers, benefit case numbers, and login codes private.
Use a City storage center for belongings and the Think Dignity ID Bank for vital-document storage when eligible. Medication cannot be stored in City storage bins.

categories.title: Domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, and protection

entries.title: YWCA Becky's House — domestic-violence shelter
entries.description:
24-hour hotline: 619-234-3164.
Confidential safety planning, crisis counseling, and emergency shelter for adults and children of all genders escaping domestic violence. Intake is available 24 hours, but space is not guaranteed. Do not share a confidential shelter location.
YWCA San Diego County — domestic-violence services

entries.title: Center for Community Solutions
entries.description:
24-hour hotline: 888-385-4657.
Confidential support for domestic violence and sexual assault, including crisis counseling, safety planning, shelter screening, legal advocacy, and referrals. Call 911 if the danger is immediate.
San Diego Superior Court — verified regional hotline list

entries.title: Your Safe Place — central support hub
entries.description:
Phone: 619-533-6000.
One location for advocacy, restraining-order help, legal information, immigration assistance, safety planning, and connections for survivors of violence or abuse. Services are confidential; call before visiting when safety is a concern.
City of San Diego — Your Safe Place

entries.title: National Human Trafficking Hotline
entries.description:
Call: 888-373-7888. Text: 233733.
For forced labor, commercial sexual exploitation, withheld documents, threats, or control by another person. Do not confront a trafficker. Call 911 for immediate danger.
National Human Trafficking Hotline

entries.title: Adult Protective Services
entries.description:
24-hour hotline: 800-510-2020.
Report suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or financial exploitation of an older adult or dependent adult in San Diego County. Call 911 when danger is immediate.
County of San Diego — protection hotlines

entries.title: Child Abuse Hotline
entries.description:
24-hour hotline: 800-344-6000.
Report suspected child abuse, sexual abuse, exploitation, or a child without adequate care. For a child or teenager who needs a safe place tonight, also call San Diego Youth Services at 866-752-2327. Call 911 for immediate danger.
County of San Diego — child-protection hotline

categories.title: Families, youth, LGBTQ+ people, older adults, and disability needs

entries.title: Families with children
entries.description:
Call 211 and say that dependent children are with you. Ask for family-specific outreach and coordinated intake. Father Joe's Villages Joan Kroc Center and Alpha Project Family Shelter are major access points, but neither guarantees same-day placement.
Alpha Project — Family Shelter | Father Joe's Villages — family access — https://my.neighbor.org/get-help/

entries.title: Minors ages 12–17
entries.description:
San Diego Youth Services screening: 866-752-2327, 24 hours.
Call for shelter, drop-in support, and safety planning. State if there is abuse, exploitation, medical need, or no safe adult. The program is voluntary and telephone screening is required.
Youth Emergency Shelter information

entries.title: Transition-age youth ages 18–24
entries.description:
Ask 211 specifically for a transition-age youth shelter or outreach team. Options include Safe STAY and Urban Street Angels; both depend on current capacity and intake.
SDHC — current youth programs

entries.title: San Diego LGBT Community Center
entries.description:
Main phone: 619-692-2077. Safe STAY bed inquiry: 619-694-6182.
LGBTQ-affirming housing navigation, homelessness prevention, shelter for ages 18–24, host homes, adult housing services, and referrals. Program eligibility and openings vary.
The Center — housing services

entries.title: Serving Seniors
entries.description:
Phone: 619-235-6572.
Meals, social services, health and benefit navigation, housing support, and referrals for older adults. Serving Seniors currently warns that it does not offer immediate emergency housing, so call 211 for a same-night shelter need.
Serving Seniors — current services and meals
entries.address: Address: 1525 4th Avenue, San Diego, CA 92101

entries.title: Aging & Independence Services
entries.description:
Phone: 800-339-4661.
County information and referral for older adults and adults with disabilities, including in-home support, benefits, caregiver support, food, protection, and community services. Ask for accessible communication or interpretation if needed.
County of San Diego — HHSA contacts

entries.title: Disability and accessibility needs
entries.description:
Tell 211, outreach, and shelter staff before placement if you need wheelchair access, a lower bunk, refrigeration or secure storage for medication, oxygen, a personal-care attendant, sign-language interpretation, or accommodation for a service animal.
If a housing provider refuses a reasonable accommodation, call Legal Aid at 877-534-2524. An accommodation request does not guarantee a specific bed when none is available.
Legal Aid Society — disability and housing help

entries.title: Students and families without stable housing
entries.description:
San Diego Unified's homeless-education program can help eligible students remain enrolled, arrange transport to school, obtain meals and supplies, and connect families with services. Ask the school for its McKinney-Vento liaison.
San Diego Unified — homeless and foster support

entries.title: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
entries.description:
Phone: 877-424-3838, free and confidential, 24 hours.
For veterans who are homeless or at risk, and for family, friends, or providers helping a veteran. Ask for connection to local VA housing, health, food, employment, and justice services.
VA Homeless Programs — get help

entries.title: VA San Diego homeless-veteran care
entries.description:
Local homeless-veteran line: 619-497-8989.
Local coordinators can help with immediate shelter and food, transitional and permanent housing, job training, justice-system navigation, financial support, addiction and mental-health treatment, and medical or dental care.
VA San Diego — homeless-veteran care

entries.title: Veterans Village of San Diego
entries.description:
Program entry: 619-393-2000. Housing information: 619-508-8866. Rapid rehousing and prevention: call or text 619-339-0111.
Veteran shelter, transitional and permanent housing, employment, behavioral health, legal support, and rapid rehousing. Eligibility, discharge documentation, income limits, referral, and capacity vary by program.
VVSD — housing programs
entries.address: Address: 4141 Pacific Highway, San Diego, CA 92110

entries.title: Tell shelter staff about the animal before referral
entries.description:
State whether the animal is a trained service animal or a pet, its size and species, vaccination status, behavior around people and animals, and whether you have a carrier, leash, food, and medication. Ask for the rule in writing when possible.
Do not abandon an animal because of an unconfirmed placement. The South County Lighthouse says it may accept up to two pets, and some safe-parking or safe-sleeping options may have different rules. Confirm directly before traveling.

entries.title: San Diego Humane Society Community Pet Pantry
entries.description:
Phone: 619-299-7012. San Diego campus: 5500 Gaines Street, San Diego, CA 92110.
The Humane Society publishes pet-food and supply pickup Tuesday–Sunday, 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m., without an appointment, while supplies last. Call before traveling and ask about alternatives if transport is difficult.
San Diego Humane Society — community support

entries.title: Community veterinary help
entries.description:
Phone: 619-299-7012. Ask for the Community Veterinary Program.
Ask about current low-cost or assistance-based veterinary services, vaccination, spay or neuter, and emergency resources. Availability, residency, and income rules can change; calling does not guarantee treatment or payment.
San Diego Humane Society — Resource Center

entries.title: Animal Safehouse for domestic-violence survivors
entries.description:
Rancho Coastal Humane Society: 760-753-6413.
The San Diego Superior Court lists this confidential animal-safehouse resource for people escaping domestic violence. Call a domestic-violence advocate first when possible so safety planning includes both the survivor and the animal.
San Diego Superior Court — domestic-violence resources

entries.title: Verification and corrections
entries.description:
This page uses government, public-agency, and provider sources. Dynamic shelter availability, referral routes, distribution schedules, and funding must be confirmed on the day help is needed.
Found a closed service, wrong phone number, or useful local resource? See how to contribute or report incorrect information. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
